title: Agent Certificate v0 Signature and Co-Attestation Wire Shapes
description: Issuer-signature scope and client co-attestation block for Agent Certificate v0. Both sign the canonical manifest BYTES, not the manifest digest: client signed bytes are UTF8(`traigent.agent_certificate.client_co_attestation.v0`) || 0x00 || uint64be(len(manifest_jcs_bytes)) || manifest_jcs_bytes; issuer signed bytes are UTF8(`traigent.agent_certificate.issuer_signature.v0`) || 0x00 || uint64be(len(manifest_jcs_bytes)) || manifest_jcs_bytes || uint64be(len(co_signature_raw)) || co_signature_raw. `co_signature_raw` is strict RFC 4648 base64-decoded signature bytes and is empty when absent. The signed_payload discriminator must agree with zero/nonzero co-signature length. The manifest_digest remains a transmitted digest/reference and is not the signature preimage. This family does NOT reuse ArtifactSignatureEnvelopeV2 — reuse was struck because adding nested signatures and new fields changes the format and verifier. The v0 issuer path is a dedicated per-environment certificate-signing key through protected GitHub-OIDC CI; the trust ring must be a signed, versioned artifact whose root fingerprint is pinned in the independent verifier. SCHEMA-1 P0 FIX: UnsignedManifestRefV0 carries the complete typed manifest document alongside its digest and fixed coverage list. Root instance is one CertificateSignaturesV0.

UnsignedManifestCoverageV0.description: The FIXED coverage list of the canonical unsigned manifest — the twelve sections C6 Ruling 3(iv) enumerates plus the signed disclosure-profile binding, pinned as a const so a manifest that covers less is unrepresentable. Freshness data is covered material; per-certificate expiry semantics are pinned by the signed semantics manifest. SCHEMA-1 (2026-08-25): certificate_unsigned_manifest_v0_schema.json#/definitions/UnsignedManifestV0 is the typed document these twelve labels name — each label is a required property of that object with concrete canonical preimage data, closing gap C1 ('coverage is a label, not a binding') and the mutable disclosure-profile gap. This file does not $ref that document (avoiding a dependency cycle back through this file's own consumers); the correspondence is enforced by keeping this const list and UnsignedManifestV0's required-property list identical, checked in tests/test_agent_certificate_v0_schemas.py.

UnsignedManifestRefV0.description: The canonical unsigned manifest AS TRANSMITTED (SCHEMA-1 P0 fix, 2026-08-25): `document` is the complete typed certificate_unsigned_manifest_v0_schema.json#/definitions/UnsignedManifestV0 object, including the signed disclosure-profile projection. `manifest_digest` is computed over that complete content-free document; an independent verifier now needs no issuer database to obtain the manifest it is checking a signature over.

CoAttestationV0.description: The client co-attestation block. The client signs the complete canonical issuer-signed certificate projection, never a digest and never a spine, with only this outer co_attestation member excluded. The projection includes the audit report's ordered rows, evidence_basis values, abstentions, claims, and issuer signature. `signed_manifest_digest` is a transmitted role-domain digest of that projection; the verifier recomputes it and never trusts the transmitted value. The project-scoped client key reference crosses as ClientKeyRefV0, not raw public-key bytes. NONCE BINDING: `nonce` MUST equal the manifest's freshness.nonce; a verifier compares both values after decoding the transmitted document.

client_key_ref.description: Opaque reference to the enrolled client signing key. A stable pseudonymous identifier with a linkability cost (C1, tension T3); never raw public-key bytes in v0.

signed_manifest_digest.description: Role-domain digest of the canonical issuer-signed certificate projection with only the outer co_attestation member removed. The verifier recomputes this value from the received certificate and rejects omissions or tampering.

nonce.description: Public anti-replay nonce. Register entry 8 wording travels verbatim: a public nonce 'does not prevent dictionary guessing.'

IssuerSignatureV0.description: The issuer signature. The issuer signs the exact canonical manifest BYTES followed by a length-delimited raw co-signature: UTF8(`traigent.agent_certificate.issuer_signature.v0`) || 0x00 || uint64be(len(manifest_jcs_bytes)) || manifest_jcs_bytes || uint64be(len(co_signature_raw)) || co_signature_raw. `co_signature_raw` is strict RFC 4648 base64-decoded bytes and is zero length when no co-attestation exists. `signed_payload` names whether that final length is zero or nonzero; the enclosing CertificateSignaturesV0 enforces the same discriminator for the presence/absence of the block. The signing workflow must verify the finalized manifest and ledger before signing; this shape does not prove that workflow. ECDSA P-256 signatures use fixed IEEE-P1363 r||s and the verifier rejects high-S. KEY-REF BINDING: issuer_key_ref and trust_ring_ref MUST equal the manifest's key-ring identifiers.

issuer_key_ref.description: Opaque reference to the dedicated per-environment certificate-signing key. Never the development Planner key; the general backend pod holds no certificate-signing authority (C6 Ruling 4, binding).

trust_ring_ref.description: Opaque reference to the signed, versioned trust-ring artifact (with version) under which the issuer key is published. Offline verification additionally needs 'a compiled minimum checkpoint or another pinned release policy' against rollback (C6 Ruling 4) — a verifier obligation, not representable here.

signed_payload.description: The issuer always signs the unsigned manifest first. A client co-attestation is a subsequent signature over the complete issuer-signed certificate projection and is not included in the issuer preimage.

CertificateSignaturesV0.description: The complete signature block: canonical unsigned-manifest reference, optional client co-attestation, and the issuer signature. When a co-attestation is present the issuer signature MUST cover it (signed_payload = [unsigned_manifest, co_attestation]); when absent it MUST NOT claim to. 'Missing co-attestation should refuse issuance' for any tier-1 claim — that refusal is enforced at the certificate envelope (tier-1 claims require this block's co_attestation), not silently downgraded.
